item.title: [Pioneerinstitute] Massachusetts’ Declining Unemployment Rate is the Result of a Shrinking Labor Force
item.description:
At first glance, the latest unemployment numbers for Massachusetts look like good news. The state’s unemployment rate fell to 4.3 percent in August, its lowest level since March 2025 and down from a recent high of 4.8 percent in February, according to data released September 18 by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

But a falling unemployment rate doesn’t always signal a stronger labor market. A closer look shows that Massachusetts employers are still cutting jobs, and that unemployment is falling mainly because fewer residents are working or looking for work at all.

The post Massachusetts’ Declining Unemployment Rate is the Result of a Shrinking Labor Force appeared first on Pioneer Institute.

item.title: [Itrfoundation] Iowa Small Businesses Weigh In on Taxpayer Protections
item.description:

In a recent guest article for the Cedar Rapids Gazette, Cody Carlson, Iowa state director of the National Federation of Independent Business (NFIB), explained why Amendment One matters to the thousands of small businesses that help drive Iowa's economy.  NFIB represents more than 10,000 small and independent business owners across Iowa, and its members have expressed overwhelming support for Amendment One.
